title: Synchronizing Beliefs with Second-Order Theory-of-Mind in Human-Autonomy Teams (Extended Version)
abstract: arXiv:2608.11229v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Comparative feedback, asking people which of two behaviors they prefer, has become a standard way to align robot and agent behavior with human intent when the reward itself cannot be specified directly. Preference-based reward learning typically casts the human teacher as a passive oracle answering learner-generated queries. We argue this forfeits the teacher's defining advantage: knowledge of the objective. A teacher who knows the target can construct training examples more efficiently than any learner-driven acquisition strategy, an advantage that widens as the reward's feature dimension grows. However, exploiting this advantage requires an accurate model of what the learner currently knows. We therefore recast preference learning as a human-autonomy team problem coupling two behavioral models: the teacher maintains a model of the learner to design an informative curriculum, and the learner maintains a second-order model of the teacher

translated_title: 在人机自主团队中通过二阶心智理论同步信念（扩展版）
translated_abstract: 比较反馈，即询问人们偏好两种行为中的哪一种，已成为在无法直接指定奖励时，使机器人和智能体行为与人类意图对齐的标准方法。基于偏好的奖励学习通常将人类教师视为一个被动的“神谕”，仅回答学习者生成的查询。我们认为这放弃了教师的核心优势：对目标的知识。知道目标的教师能够比任何学习者驱动的采集策略更高效地构建训练示例，这种优势随着奖励特征维度的增长而扩大。然而，利用这一优势需要对学习者当前所知有准确的模型。因此，我们将偏好学习重新定义为一个耦合两种行为模型的人机自主团队问题：教师维护一个关于学习者的模型以设计信息丰富的课程，而学习者维护一个关于教师的二阶模型。
tldr: 本文提出将偏好学习重塑为人机自主团队问题，通过教师和学习者各自维护对对方的模型（教师建模学习者、学习者二阶建模教师），以利用教师对目标的知识更高效地构建训练示例，从而提升奖励学习效率。
en_tdlr: This paper reframes preference learning as a human-autonomy team problem where the teacher models the learner to design informative curricula and the learner maintains a second-order model of the teacher, exploiting the teacher's knowledge of the objective for more efficient reward learning.
